1.1.listen: Trace the melody with your hand while it plays: up when it climbs, down when it falls. That's pitch.
1.1.guitar: Play the low E string open, then the high E string open. Same letter, two octaves apart in pitch.

songs.title: Golden
songs.artist: HUNTR/X, EJAE, AUDREY NUNA, REI AMI & KPop Demon Hunters Cast

1.2.listen: Hum the first note of the chorus, then find it on your guitar and name its letter, A to G.
1.2.guitar: Play the open strings from low to high and say each letter out loud: E A D G B E.

1.3.listen: Sing the hook, then sing it again higher or lower until it's comfortable. Same notes in a different octave.
1.3.guitar: Play A on the open A string, then A at fret 2 of the G string. They're an octave apart.

1.4.listen: While it plays, try F and then F♯ on your guitar. One of them clashes and one fits. A sharp is one fret higher.
1.4.guitar: On the high E string, F is fret 1 and F♯ is fret 2. One fret is one half step.

1.5.listen: Find the song's home note on your guitar. If that fret is a sharp or flat, give it both of its names.
1.5.guitar: Fret 4 on the A string is C♯, and it's also D♭. One fret, two names.

songs.title: On The Ground
songs.note: In D♭ major. D♭ is also called C♯.

2.1.listen: Slide one finger up a string one fret at a time while it plays. Each fret is a half step. Stop when a note fits the song.
2.1.guitar: On the B string, fret 1 to fret 2 is a half step, and fret 1 to fret 3 is a whole step.

2.2.listen: Find the home note, then sing do-re-mi up from it. If the scale fits the song, the song is in a major key.
2.2.guitar: Play the C major scale in open position: C (A string, fret 3), D, E, F, G, A, B, C.

songs.title: we can't be friends (wait for your love)

2.3.listen: Each of these is in a major key. Count the flats in its key signature.
2.3.guitar: Put a capo on fret 1 and play the open C major scale. Now you're playing D♭ major, with five flats.

songs.title: On The Ground
songs.note: D♭ major: 5 flats (B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭ G♭).

3.1.listen: Play a minor song and a major song back to back. The minor one has a lowered 3rd, so home sounds darker.
3.1.guitar: Strum Am, then A. The only change is one note: the 3rd, C or C♯.

songs.title: Lovesick Girls
songs.note: Chorus loops D♯m, C♯, F♯, B. Does it feel at home on D♯m or F♯?

3.2.listen: Relative keys share a key signature. Every major key has a minor key that starts on its 6th note.
3.2.guitar: Put a capo on fret 4 and strum Bm, A, D, G. Those shapes sound as Lovesick Girls' D♯m, C♯, F♯, B.

songs.title: good 4 u
songs.note: F♯ minor has 3 sharps, the same as its relative, A major.

songs.title: drivers license
songs.note: B♭ major, but it ends on G minor, its relative minor.

songs.title: Lovesick Girls
songs.note: D♯ minor and F♯ major share 6 sharps.

3.3.listen: Hum the home note (the tonic), then the note five steps above it (the dominant). Hear how the dominant wants to go home?
3.3.guitar: In A minor: play A (open A string), then E (open low E string or fret 2 on the D string). Tonic, then dominant.

4.1.listen: Count 1, 2, 3, 4 along with the beat. Where does your count start over? That's the start of a bar.
4.1.guitar: Strum Em down on every beat, 4 strums per bar, and count out loud.

4.2.listen: Clap along with the kick drum, then try clapping twice as fast. You've gone from quarter notes to eighth notes.
4.2.guitar: Hold Em for 4 beats (a whole note), then strum it 2, 4 and 8 times in the same space.

4.3.listen: Find a note the singer holds in the chorus. Count how many beats it lasts. Longer than one value? That's a dot or a tie.
4.3.guitar: Strum G, let it ring for 1½ beats (a dotted quarter), then strum again on the 'and' of 2.

4.4.listen: Tap the beat. Does it feel like 1-2, 1-2 or like 1-2-3, 1-2-3? That's the meter.
4.4.guitar: Strum C as a waltz (1-2-3), then in 4 (1-2-3-4). Feel how different they are.

4.5.listen: Try fitting three even claps into one beat of the song. That's a triplet: three in the space of two.
4.5.guitar: Mute the strings with your fretting hand and strum three even strokes per beat: tri-pl-et, tri-pl-et.

4.6.listen: Write the rhythm of the hook's first bar so each beat is easy to see. Group the notes beat by beat.
4.6.guitar: Play the hook's rhythm on one muted string while counting the beats out loud.

5.1.listen: Sing the first two notes of the chorus. Count the letter names from one to the other, both included. That's the interval's size.
5.1.guitar: On the A string, fret 0 to fret 2 is a 2nd (A to B), and fret 0 to fret 4 is a 3rd (A to C♯).

5.2.listen: Hum the home note, then the highest note of the hook. Count up the major scale from home to name the interval.
5.2.guitar: A perfect 5th: the open A string, then fret 2 on the D string (E).

5.3.listen: Pick a note from the hook and build a major 3rd above it on your guitar. Does it fit the song?
5.3.guitar: Major 3rd: fret 3 on the A string (C), then fret 2 on the D string (E).

5.4.listen: Sing a leap up from the hook, then sing it with the top note dropped an octave. The interval flips: a 3rd becomes a 6th.
5.4.guitar: C up to E is a 3rd (A string fret 3, D string fret 2). E up to C is a 6th (D string fret 2, B string fret 1). 3 + 6 = 9.

songs.title: hate that i made you love me

5.5.listen: Listen for a tense, edgy spot in the song. Augmented and diminished intervals, like the tritone, often make that sound.
5.5.guitar: A tritone: the open A string with fret 1 on the D string (D♯). Then resolve to E (D string, fret 2).

6.1.listen: Find one chord that fits the chorus, then name its root, 3rd and 5th.
6.1.guitar: Strum C, then play its notes one at a time: C (A string, fret 3), E (D string, fret 2), G (open G).

6.2.listen: Look up the song's chords and read each symbol: a plain letter is major, m is minor, ° is diminished, + is augmented.
6.2.guitar: Strum C, then Cm (barre at fret 3, Am shape). Hear the 3rd drop a half step.

6.3.listen: Listen to the bass. Does it always play the chord's root, or does it sometimes sit on the 3rd or 5th? That's an inversion.
6.3.guitar: Play C/E: the open C shape, but strum from the open low E string so E is in the bass.

6.4.listen: Pick one chord from the song and name three things: its root, its quality and its bass note.
6.4.guitar: Strum Am and name it: root A, minor, A in the bass. Then play it from the low E string: Am/E.

6.5.listen: Listen for a chord that sounds open and unsettled before it lands. Swapping the 3rd for a 4th or 2nd makes that sus sound.
6.5.guitar: Strum D, then Dsus4 (fret 3 on the high E string), then back to D.
